note.en: Two sleeves are allowed as an attacking grip. Holding both sleeve ends for defence, or screwing them up, draws a shido.

about.en: Both hands on the sleeves, one of them lifted high. It gives up the lapel and with it the posture control, and gets in return a lifting hand that can raise the whole arm: the sleeve-lifting hip throw is the throw it exists for, and the side circle throw from the same lift.

en: Both grips above the elbow, not at the cuff
One sleeve lifts, the other pulls; they never do the same job
Change to it late, from a grip already established
From the sleeve grip, let go of the lapel and take your partner's other sleeve with your lifting hand, above the elbow.
Lift that sleeve high, so their arm rises and their shoulder with it.
Pull the other sleeve down and across your hip.
Turn in under the lifted arm.

receiving.en: Both your sleeves held and one arm being lifted means a hip throw under the lifted arm, or a foot in your stomach. Drop the lifted elbow and take a lapel with the free hand before the lift is complete.

viNotes.en: Losing the lapel grip on your partner tells you they have gone to two sleeves before you feel the lift. The lifted arm is the side the throw comes from.
